title: Classification of groups of order p^3

problemStatement.formal: For a prime p, up to isomorphism there are exactly five groups of order p^3 when p is odd: the abelian C_{p^3}, C_{p^2} x C_p, C_p x C_p x C_p, and the non-abelian Heisenberg group Heis(p) = <a,b,c | a^p=b^p=c^p=1, [a,b]=c, [a,c]=[b,c]=1> (exponent p) and the modular group M_{p^3} = <a,b | a^{p^2}=b^p=1, b^{-1}ab=a^{1+p}> (exponent p^2); for p=2 the two non-abelian groups are D_4 and Q_8.
problemStatement.plain: Groups of order p^2 are always abelian, but p^3 is the smallest order at which a prime-power group can be non-abelian. The goal is to prove the full classification: three abelian groups (from the partitions of 3) and two non-abelian ones. For odd p the non-abelian pair is the Heisenberg group of exponent p and the modular group of exponent p^2; the prime p=2 is exceptional, giving D_4 and Q_8 instead.
whyMatters: It is the natural next rung after the order-p^2 classification and the first case exhibiting genuinely non-abelian p-group structure (center of order p, commutator subgroup equal to the center, rank-2 Frattini quotient).
The exponent-p non-abelian model is the prototypical extraspecial group, which recurs across representation theory, central extensions, and quantum information (the Heisenberg/Pauli group).

proven: Groups of order p^2 are abelian and split into the cyclic / elementary-abelian dichotomy (gallery proof group-order-prime-squared-abelian-oq-01).
Finite abelian groups are classified as products of cyclic prime-power groups (Mathlib finite abelian structure theorem), pinning down the three abelian classes of order p^3.
Every p-group has a nontrivial center (IsPGroup.center_nontrivial), the seed of the non-abelian analysis.
Mathlib provides the p=2 non-abelian representatives D_4 and Q_8, and Heisenberg-type group constructions.
open: No Lean formalization enumerates the five isomorphism classes of order p^3 and proves the list is exhaustive and non-redundant.
The exponent invariant exp(G) in {p, p^2} as the discriminator between the two non-abelian classes is not packaged for general odd p.
The p=2 special case (D_4 vs Q_8) versus odd p needs a unified or case-split treatment linked to this classification.
Explicit MulEquiv isomorphisms between an abstract order-p^3 group and the named representatives are missing.
knownResults.goal: First milestone (odd p): prove a non-abelian group of order p^3 has |Z(G)| = p with Z(G) = [G,G] = Phi(G), G/Z(G) isomorphic to C_p x C_p (extraspecial), and is determined up to isomorphism by its exponent (p or p^2), yielding exactly two non-abelian classes; combined with Mathlib's abelian classification this gives the count of five. Explicit MulEquiv to concrete presentations is a stretch goal.
